clue.text: Former Anglican novice needs to do better

parts.note: ex- means former, as in an ex-partner
CE stands for Church of England, the Anglican church
L is a learner, as on the L-plates of a learner driver

explanation.surface: An ex-Anglican trainee is told they must improve.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass others or perform outstandingly is to outdo them, so it fits doing better.

clue.text: The evolution of giant mice is puzzling

indicators.note: evolution is gradual change, so the letters of giant mice change their order

explanation.surface: How large rodents came about is a scientific mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mysterious or baffling is puzzling.

clue.text: Study by well-established landscape artist

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
stable means firmly established

explanation.surface: A respected painter of the countryside is studied closely.
explanation.walkthrough: John Constable was the English painter of rural landscapes such as The Hay Wain.
explanation.definitionFit: The English painter of rural Suffolk scenes is famed for landscape art.

clue.text: What an early prankster gets up to and with!

definitions.text: What an early prankster gets up to and with!

parts.words: What an early prankster gets up to and with!
parts.note: a songbird famous for rising at dawn, and also a mischievous prank that a joker gets up to

explanation.surface: A joker who rises early and gets into mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up with the ...' is the idiom for rising early, and the same word means a prank, so it is what a prankster gets up to.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird that sings at dawn gives the idiom for early rising, and the word also means a playful prank.

clue.text: Non-white international rugby side

parts.note: read literally, a team dressed entirely in black with no white kit; really New Zealand's famous national rugby team

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a rugby team by its players' race.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Zealand rugby union team is known for its all-black strip, so 'Non-white' describes the kit, not the players.
explanation.definitionFit: New Zealand's national rugby union team takes its nickname from its black jerseys.

clue.text: One of Shaw's dramas man then produced

indicators.note: the letters of dramas man then are produced in a fresh arrangement, as a play is produced

explanation.surface: A play by George Bernard Shaw being staged.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw's 1894 comedy takes its title from Virgil's opening line, 'Of arms and the man I sing'.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw wrote this comedy about a Swiss mercenary, one of his plays.

clue.text: Behold a holy man-in the wilderness?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning behold or look
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: Look at a hermit-saint living out in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone astray in a wilderness has no idea where they are.

clue.text: Elected to write article in French

definitions.meaning: past tense of picking or opting for something
the French word for a thing or object, an article

explanation.surface: A politician voted in decides to write a piece in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Opted or picked is the English sense; in French it is the word for a thing, an article.

clue.text: The lady is going to pod peas

parts.note: she refers to a lady
'll is the short form of will, meaning is going to

explanation.surface: A woman about to remove peas from their pods.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking peas out of their husks is to remove their casing.

clue.text: Pub known as The Queen next to The Bull

parts.note: an inn is a pub
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's Queen

explanation.surface: A pub called The Queen stands beside one called The Bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Bull' looks like another pub sign, but it is the bull's-eye of a target, and the ring around it is the one meant.
explanation.definitionFit: On a dartboard or archery target, the ring immediately surrounding the bull's-eye has this name.

clue.text: John Stuart's style proves a great handicap

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was the Victorian philosopher, so 'John Stuart's' gives Mill's
tone means style or manner, as in the tone of a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A Victorian philosopher's writing style is a real burden to readers.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy stone for grinding grain hung round one's neck is the proverbial burden, an encumbrance.

clue.text: A fellow barrister

parts.note: the courteous phrase barristers use in court for another member of their profession

explanation.surface: Just describes another lawyer at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: In British courts a barrister refers to opposing counsel by a set polite phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The courtroom form of address for another barrister is this phrase.

clue.text: In the army that's a tradition

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words army that's, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Something every soldier claims is an old regimental custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend or traditional story passed down through generations is a kind of tradition.

clue.text: German agreement to search for gold in the Far East

parts.note: ja is German for yes
to pan is to wash river gravel in a pan looking for gold

explanation.surface: A German says yes to prospecting for gold somewhere in East Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The island nation is one of the chief countries of the Far East, standing here for the region.

clue.text: Brother's room is 145 inches

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, leaving 45 inches
an ell is an old measure of cloth, 45 inches long

explanation.surface: A monk's sleeping quarters are given an oddly exact measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 145 inches as 100 plus 45 inches: C is the Roman 100 and the ell, an old cloth measure, is 45 inches.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother here is a monk, whose small private room in a monastery has this name.

clue.text: Welsh poet heartened by one TV producer

indicators.note: the poet is given one as its heart, so it goes in the middle

parts.note: a bard is a poet, especially in Welsh tradition
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Welsh poet is cheered by a television maker.
explanation.walkthrough: John Logie Baird, a Scottish engineer, gave the first demonstration of television in 1926.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish inventor who first demonstrated a working television is the producer of TV meant.

clue.text: A step taken quickly

parts.note: a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: Someone strides out briskly.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving at speed, swiftly, is what this old adverb means.

clue.text: They seize a vessel at a guest-house celebration

parts.note: a boarding house is a guest-house, so boarding stands in for it
a party is a celebration

explanation.surface: Pirates hold a celebration at a seaside guest-house.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of sailors who climb aboard and capture an enemy ship are given this name.

clue.text: Exercise during leisure period calls for moderation

indicators.note: exercise happens during the rest period, so it goes inside it

parts.note: a rest is a period of leisure
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: Working out during a break calls for not overdoing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding back and keeping oneself in check is moderation.

clue.text: Standard London policeman's baton

parts.note: the Yard, Scotland Yard, is the London Metropolitan Police headquarters
a stick is a baton

explanation.surface: A London police officer's regulation truncheon.
explanation.definitionFit: A measuring rod one yard long gives the word for any measure or criterion of comparison.

clue.text: Sell all the turntables and prepare for action

definitions.meaning: read literally, to clear out all one's record decks
naval idiom for removing clutter from a warship's decks before battle

explanation.definitionFit: Getting ready for a big task by removing obstacles, from warships readying for battle, and humorously emptying a DJ's record players.

clue.text: A broken piece in the computer

definitions.meaning: a small fragment knocked off something, as from a cup
a silicon microchip inside a computer

explanation.definitionFit: A fragment broken off china, and also the small integrated circuit wafer at a computer's heart.

clue.text: Detectives hesitate to have a drink

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Detectives hesitate before accepting a drink on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic drink made from fermented apples.

clue.text: Mali's established religion

indicators.note: the letters of Mali's are set up in a new order, established afresh

explanation.surface: The official faith of the West African country of Mali.
explanation.walkthrough: 'established religion' reads as a state faith, but 'established' signals rearranging MALIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muslim faith is a world religion, and indeed the majority one in Mali.

clue.text: Sergeant-Major has to hand out weapons and grease the locks

parts.note: to arm troops is to issue them with weapons

explanation.surface: A sergeant-major distributes weapons and then oils his hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' looks like door locks, but means hair: to smarm is to slick hair down with oil.
explanation.definitionFit: To plaster one's hair down with oil or pomade is this verb's literal sense.

clue.text: Votes for having image-makers

definitions.meaning: the arguments or votes in favour
Public relations officers, who manage a client's image

explanation.definitionFit: Points or votes in favour, and also public relations officers who shape a public image.

clue.text: Bearing north-east up to the motorway

indicators.note: the reversed piece is added on to the end of the motorway

parts.note: M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: Giving a compass direction toward the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's demeanour or carriage, their manner, is their bearing.

clue.text: Melbourne meat producer

definitions.meaning: Lord Melbourne, Victoria's first Prime Minister
a young sheep, which gives tender meat

explanation.definitionFit: The family name of Lord Melbourne, the Victorian Prime Minister, and a young sheep reared for meat.

clue.text: Democrat coalition is a waste of time

parts.note: an alliance is a coalition of parties or nations

explanation.surface: A political pact involving a Democrat achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle trifling or loitering about is time frittered away.

clue.text: Bail arranged before one gets proof of innocence

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come before the next piece
the letters of bail are arranged into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A suspect gets bail arranged and then evidence clearing their name.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea of having been elsewhere when a crime occurred is the classic evidence of innocence.

clue.text: No drama or production made the old way

indicators.note: a production makes something new out of materials, so these words are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre group stages no play at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' looks like a theatre staging alongside 'drama', but signals the rearrangement of NO DRAMA OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight highway built across the empire in antiquity is literally an old way, way meaning road.

clue.text: Printed fabric Christopher and Jack brought back

indicators.note: both names are written then read from the end back to the start

parts.note: Kit is a short form of the name Christopher
a jack tar is a sailor, and AB, able seaman, is too

explanation.surface: Two men return from abroad with printed cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses the whole run KITAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Wax-resist dyeing produces patterned cloth, an Indonesian textile technique.
